english.title: Occupy a building on which a demolition order is operative
english.standardoffencewording: On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) knowing that a demolition order had become operative and applied to premises at **(..SPECIFY ADDRESS..), entered into occupation of the premises, or part of them, after the date by which the order required them to be vacated
english.legislation: Contrary to section 270(5)(a) of the Housing Act 1985.
english.pointstoprove:
date and location
knowing that a demolition order became operative and applied to premises
entered into occupation of the premises, or a part of them, after the date by which the order required them to be vacated, /
permitted another person to enter into such occupation after that date

investigatoraction.description: Guilty Plea by letter procedure may be offered for this offence
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.standardstatementoffacts: On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) the defendant, knowing that a demolition order had become operative and applied to premises at **(..SPECIFY ADDRESS..), the defendant entered into occupation of the premises, or part of them, after the date by which the order required them to be vacated.

other.penalty:
Summary-A fine not exceeding level five on the standard scale and a further fine not exceeding £5 for every day or part of a day on which the occupation continues after conviction.Time limit for prosecutions:
6 months

Note
On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates’ court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.

libra.complexpenaltydetails: A fine not exceeding level five on the standard scale and to a further fine not exceeding £5 for every day or part of a day on which the occupation continues after conviction.
